present-simple-vs-continuous-prompt-1.instructions: Write three pairs of sentences. In each pair, use the present simple for a routine or general truth and the present continuous for an action in progress or a temporary situation.
present-simple-vs-continuous-prompt-1.starterText: She works in the office, but this week she is working from home.
present-simple-vs-continuous-prompt-1.modelAnswer: They usually take the train to work, but today they are driving because of the strike. My brother studies economics at university, but this month he is studying for his final exams every evening. We often eat at home on weekdays, but tonight we are eating out with some friends.

present-simple-vs-continuous-2-prompt-1.instructions: Rewrite five sentences and choose the more natural tense. Use the present simple for stative verbs unless the sentence clearly emphasizes temporary behaviour or change.
present-simple-vs-continuous-2-prompt-1.starterText: I understand the problem, but he is being unusually difficult today.
present-simple-vs-continuous-2-prompt-1.modelAnswer: I understand the problem now. He is being unusually difficult today. We know the manager quite well. She looks tired this week. They prefer remote work, but this month they are trying a hybrid schedule.

future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.instructions: Write four timeline sentences about a project. Use the future perfect for completed milestones before a future deadline and the future continuous for work that will still be happening at a specific future time.
future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.starterText: By Thursday, the analysts will have finished the budget review, and at 3 p.m. the finance lead will be presenting the revised figures to the board.
future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.modelAnswer: By next Monday, the design team will have completed the revised client pack. At 11 a.m. that day, the project manager will be meeting the client to discuss the final changes. By the end of the month, we will have updated the onboarding guide for the regional teams. During Friday's review session, the support lead will be explaining the rollout timeline to the new hires.

mixed-conditionals-prompt-1.instructions: Write four sentences using mixed conditionals to reflect on a past decision and its present result, or a present condition and its past consequence.
mixed-conditionals-prompt-1.starterText: If we had planned the launch more carefully, we would be in a much stronger position now.
mixed-conditionals-prompt-1.modelAnswer: If the team had tested the feature earlier, we would not be dealing with these client complaints now. If I were more confident in public speaking, I would have accepted the conference invitation last month. If the supplier had delivered on time, the product would be on the market already. If she were better at delegating, she would not have missed the earlier deadline.

inversion-for-emphasis-prompt-1.instructions: Write four formal sentences using inversion after negative or limiting expressions such as rarely, never, only then, or not until.
inversion-for-emphasis-prompt-1.starterText: Rarely have I seen a proposal generate such immediate support from senior management.
inversion-for-emphasis-prompt-1.modelAnswer: Rarely have I seen a project team recover so quickly after a major delay. Only after the audit did the board understand the full scale of the problem. Not until the final review did the client approve the revised schedule. Never had the department faced such a complex negotiation before the merger talks began.

applying-for-a-job-prompt-1.instructions: Write a short formal cover letter that introduces your application, highlights relevant experience, and explains why you are suitable for the role.
applying-for-a-job-prompt-1.starterText: Dear Hiring Manager, I am writing to apply for the entry-level marketing assistant role advertised on your website.
applying-for-a-job-prompt-1.modelAnswer: Dear Hiring Manager, I am writing to apply for the entry-level marketing assistant role advertised on your website. During my studies and internship, I developed strong communication skills and gained experience preparing social media content and supporting event planning. I am especially interested in this post because it offers excellent training and career prospects, and I believe my enthusiasm and attention to detail would make me a strong fit for your team. Please find attached my CV in support of my application. I look forward to hearing from you.

applying-for-a-job-prompt-2.instructions: List five phrases that commonly appear in job advertisements. Use authentic recruitment language rather than general business words.
applying-for-a-job-prompt-2.modelAnswer: competitive salary; excellent career prospects; full training provided; relevant prior experience required; strong communication skills

job-interviews-prompt-1.instructions: Write five realistic interview questions and a short model answer for each one. Keep the tone formal and job-focused.
job-interviews-prompt-1.starterText: I was shortlisted for an interview last week.
job-interviews-prompt-1.modelAnswer: Question: Why do you want this role? Answer: I am interested in this role because it matches my experience in customer service and offers strong career development. Question: What are your main strengths? Answer: My main strengths are communication, organisation, and the ability to work well under pressure. Question: Describe a challenge you faced. Answer: In my previous role, I had to resolve a delivery problem quickly, so I coordinated with the supplier and kept the client informed throughout. Question: How do you prepare for deadlines? Answer: I prioritise tasks, break projects into smaller steps, and communicate early if any issue may affect the deadline. Question: When could you start? Answer: My notice period is two weeks, so I could start shortly after that.

job-interviews-prompt-2.instructions: Describe a previous role in a formal interview style. Mention responsibilities, achievements, and what you learned from the experience.
job-interviews-prompt-2.starterText: In my previous role as a sales assistant, I was responsible for handling customer enquiries and supporting the store manager.
job-interviews-prompt-2.modelAnswer: In my previous role as a sales assistant, I was responsible for handling customer enquiries, organising stock, and supporting the store manager during busy periods. I also helped train new team members and contributed to a noticeable improvement in customer satisfaction scores. This experience strengthened my communication skills, taught me how to prioritise tasks under pressure, and showed me the importance of maintaining a professional attitude at all times.

job-interviews-prompt-3.instructions: Draft a short professional email accepting a job offer. Mention the role, gratitude, and your expected start arrangements.
job-interviews-prompt-3.starterText: Dear Ms Patel, thank you for offering me the position of Operations Assistant.
job-interviews-prompt-3.modelAnswer: Dear Ms Patel, thank you for offering me the position of Operations Assistant. I am pleased to accept the role and appreciate the confidence you have shown in my application. I understand that my start date will be 3 May, following my two-week notice period, and I look forward to joining the team. Please let me know if you need any further documents before then. Kind regards, Ana Torres

job-ad-analysis-prompt-1.instructions: Read the advertisement and summarize the role, the ideal candidate, and the overall tone in three or four sentences.
job-ad-analysis-prompt-1.starterText: The advertisement is for a junior operations assistant role at CityBridge Consulting.
job-ad-analysis-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The advertisement is for a junior operations assistant role that combines project support, scheduling, and report preparation. It is aimed at candidates with strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to stay calm under pressure, while making it clear that fast learning matters more than extensive experience. The tone is professional and encouraging because it highlights structured training, mentoring, and clear career progression.

interview-panel-summary-prompt-1.instructions: Listen to the panel summary and write a short summary of the final decision plus the main reservation that was raised.
interview-panel-summary-prompt-1.starterText: The panel decides to move the candidate forward, but they still want more detail about her experience with deadlines.
interview-panel-summary-prompt-1.listeningPromptText: The panel agrees that the candidate should move to the next stage because her preparation and communication were stronger than those of the other applicants. However, one interviewer still wants a clearer example of how she handles multiple deadlines under pressure.
interview-panel-summary-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The panel decides to move the candidate to the next stage because her preparation and communication are stronger than those of the other applicants. However, one interviewer still wants a clearer example of how she manages multiple deadlines. The final judgment is positive overall, but that reservation remains important.

interview-self-introduction-prompt-1.instructions: Answer aloud as if you were introducing yourself in a job interview. Mention your previous role, two responsibilities, and one strength that connects directly to the new role.
interview-self-introduction-prompt-1.starterText: In my previous role as a customer support assistant, I handled client requests, updated internal records, and learned how to communicate clearly under pressure. However, my biggest strength is staying organised while still keeping a professional tone with clients.
interview-self-introduction-prompt-1.modelAnswer: In my previous role as a customer support assistant, I managed client enquiries and coordinated follow-up tasks with the operations team. I was also responsible for updating internal records and making sure urgent issues were escalated quickly. However, the main strength I would bring to this position is clear communication, because I learned how to explain problems calmly and keep both clients and colleagues informed. That experience makes me a strong fit for a role that depends on organisation and professional communication.

future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.instructions: Write four sentences about a project timeline. Use the future perfect for milestones completed before a future point and the future continuous for work that will still be in progress at that time.
future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.starterText: By next Wednesday, the design team will have finished the client deck, and at 10 a.m. the product manager will be presenting the revised launch plan.
future-perfect-vs-future-continuous-prom.modelAnswer: By Monday morning, the engineers will have completed the final testing cycle. At the same time, the support team will be preparing the release notes for clients. By the end of the week, we will have updated the onboarding guide for the new feature. During Friday's review meeting, the operations lead will be explaining the rollout timeline to the regional managers.

meeting-minutes-analysis-prompt-1.instructions: Read the meeting minutes and summarize the final decision, the condition attached to it, and one action item in three or four sentences.
meeting-minutes-analysis-prompt-1.starterText: The minutes show that the team approved a phased launch, but only on the condition that extra support training is completed first.
meeting-minutes-analysis-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The minutes show that the team approved a phased product launch for July rather than a wider immediate rollout. However, the approval is conditional because the support team must complete extra training by mid-June. The chair also kept the first release limited to three markets so that technical issues could be managed more carefully. One concrete action item is that the support lead must prepare the training materials while marketing produces the client-facing FAQs.

deadline-renegotiation-call-prompt-1.instructions: Listen to the call summary and write a short summary of the final agreement plus the main condition attached to the revised deadline.
deadline-renegotiation-call-prompt-1.starterText: The client accepts the revised delivery date, but they insist on a written progress update before the board review.
deadline-renegotiation-call-prompt-1.listeningPromptText: The client agrees to move the delivery date to 18 June because they understand the technical issue that caused the delay. However, they make it clear that the deadline cannot slip again because the board review is scheduled for the following week. The revised agreement includes a written progress update by Tuesday and confirmation of final testing by Friday.
deadline-renegotiation-call-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The client agrees to move the delivery date to 18 June because they understand the technical issue that caused the delay. However, they make it clear that the deadline cannot slip again because the board review is scheduled for the following week. The agreement therefore includes a written progress update by Tuesday and confirmation of final testing by Friday.

project-update-briefing-prompt-1.instructions: Give a short spoken update to a manager. Mention one completed task, one task still in progress, and one risk that needs attention.
project-update-briefing-prompt-1.starterText: We have finished the first testing cycle, and we are now preparing the client documentation. However, the biggest current risk is that supplier approval may arrive later than expected.
project-update-briefing-prompt-1.modelAnswer: We have completed the first testing cycle and shared the internal results with the product lead. At the moment, the team is preparing the client documentation and updating the onboarding guide for launch. However, the main risk is that supplier approval may arrive later than expected, which could delay the final sign-off. If that happens, we will need to adjust the release sequence and keep the client informed immediately.

client-escalation-call-prompt-1.instructions: Listen to the escalation summary and explain the final concession, the immediate requirement attached to it, and the longer follow-up expectation.
client-escalation-call-prompt-1.starterText: The account manager grants a forty-eight-hour extension, but only if the project lead sends a revised plan by 5 p.m.
client-escalation-call-prompt-1.listeningPromptText: The account manager grants a forty-eight-hour extension because the client says the current delay has already affected two regional teams. However, the concession is conditional, since the project lead must send a revised implementation plan by 5 p.m. and join a follow-up call the next morning. The client also expects weekly status updates until the rollout is stable.
client-escalation-call-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The call ends with the account manager granting a forty-eight-hour extension because the client says the current delay has already affected two regional teams. However, the concession is conditional, since the project lead must send a revised implementation plan by 5 p.m. and join a follow-up call the next morning. The client also makes it clear that weekly status updates will still be expected until the rollout is stable.

handover-briefing-prompt-1.instructions: Give a spoken handover that explains what is finished, what tomorrow's priority is, and one unresolved risk the next person should monitor closely.
handover-briefing-prompt-1.starterText: I have finished the client notes and uploaded the revised schedule. Tomorrow's first priority is confirming the supplier timeline, but the unresolved risk is that legal approval may still arrive late.
handover-briefing-prompt-1.modelAnswer: I have completed the client notes, uploaded the revised schedule, and shared the latest budget comments with the operations lead. The top priority for tomorrow is confirming the supplier timeline before the regional team begins implementation. However, the main unresolved risk is that legal approval may still arrive late, which could delay the final sign-off. If that happens, the next step should be to warn the client immediately and adjust the handover plan.

vendor-status-update-call-prompt-1.instructions: Listen to the supplier update and summarize the reassuring headline, the remaining delivery risk, and the agreed next step.
vendor-status-update-call-prompt-1.starterText: Most components are on schedule, but the spare units may still be delayed by customs clearance.
vendor-status-update-call-prompt-1.listeningPromptText: The supplier says that most of the components have already left the warehouse and should still arrive on schedule by Thursday. However, the final batch of spare units is still waiting for customs clearance, so installation may begin without them if the clearance is delayed. The next step is for the supplier to confirm the customs update by noon tomorrow and arrange direct delivery to the site if necessary.
vendor-status-update-call-prompt-1.modelAnswer: The supplier says that most of the components have already left the warehouse and should still arrive on schedule by Thursday. However, the final batch of spare units is still waiting for customs clearance, so installation may begin without them if the clearance is delayed. The agreed next step is that the supplier will confirm the customs update by noon tomorrow and arrange direct delivery to the site if necessary.

stakeholder-recommendation-pitch-prompt-.instructions: Give a short spoken recommendation to senior stakeholders. State your preferred option early, justify it with one strong reason, and acknowledge one trade-off.
stakeholder-recommendation-pitch-prompt-.starterText: I recommend the phased rollout because it reduces operational risk, although it will delay the full launch by two weeks.
stakeholder-recommendation-pitch-prompt-.modelAnswer: I recommend the phased rollout because it reduces operational risk and gives the support team time to handle early issues before the wider release. The strongest reason for this option is that it protects the client experience while the team confirms that the new process is stable. However, the trade-off is that the full launch will take longer, so some commercial targets may move back by two weeks. Even so, the lower risk makes this the stronger option overall.

delay-update-email-prompt-1.instructions: Write a short professional email that explains the delay, gives the reason, apologizes once, and states the revised plan clearly.
delay-update-email-prompt-1.starterText: Dear Ms Rivera, I am writing to let you know that the delivery pack will arrive later than planned because our final approval has taken longer than expected.
delay-update-email-prompt-1.modelAnswer: Dear Ms Rivera, I am writing to let you know that the delivery pack will arrive one day later than planned because the final approval stage has taken longer than expected. I apologise for the inconvenience this may cause. We will send the revised version by Thursday afternoon and confirm receipt as soon as it is delivered. To prevent any further delay, I will also send you a progress update tomorrow morning. Kind regards, Daniel Soto
